Measured so far: E000 (template demo, 0.012 acc, 0.14 s) and E001 (airbench96-style port, 9 epochs, eager: acc 0.74297, time 9.43 s, complete, but infeasible because accuracy is below 0.753).

Mechanisms, by confidence:
1. The port is in the right regime. It reaches about 74.3% in 9 epochs at about 1.05 s/epoch, including fixed costs. My last-round point forecasts (0.745, 9.4 s) were close, so my calibration for this family is decent. Time scales roughly linearly with epochs, so about 1 s per epoch is the local rate.
2. The binding constraint is accuracy, not time. The gap to 0.753 is about 1 pp, which has to come from about 1 to 1.5 more epochs (about 10 to 15% time) or from a better recipe. Prior slope: about 0.5 to 0.8 pp per extra epoch near 9 epochs. This is extrapolated from airbench-like curves, not measured here. Because the port misses the bar, I002 takes the "otherwise 9 → 10" branch.
3. Systems wins are real but unmeasured. Compile, a fused optimizer and CUDA graphs are probably worth 5 to 20% under 4 CPU cores. Eager launch overhead at batch 1024 is moderate, and the per-step Python loop and the augmentation loop of 25 masked copies are plausible waste. Compile risks are recompiles and mode-specific eval shapes.
4. Fixed costs (the data move, the eigh whitening, the 25-way augment loop per epoch) are probably 0.3 to 0.8 s of the 9.4 s.
5. Muon, progressive resizing and EMA are uncertain. Each is likely within ±5% of baseline time at equal accuracy, and some will lose accuracy. Short schedules on 3 seeds make small effects hard to see.

Noise: not measured yet. Assumed per-seed accuracy std 0.2 to 0.4 pp, so the 3-seed mean has std about 0.15 to 0.25 pp. Time noise 1 to 2%.

Unsure: how much accuracy the epochs trade, whether the EMA gives +0.2 pp or more at 9 epochs, and whether compile helps or hurts when eval shapes are included.

forecasts.reason: Going from 9 to 10 epochs adds about 11% time and about +0.6 pp; this is a coin flip to clear 0.753.
Compile plus fused SGD likely saves about 10%, but max-autotune adds risk and the extra shapes may leak cost.
EMA in short schedules gives a small gain of about 0.3 pp, which is near noise, and the time cost is about 2%.
A rerun should land within about 2% on time, and per-seed std should be around 0.25 pp.
The epoch is 48 full batches plus a ragged one, so dropping the last batch changes little; the 0.3 s gain is unlikely to be detectable against compile variance.
Muon needs tuning and Newton-Schulz adds cost at width 576; it probably does not beat tuned SGD within one try.
Lower resolution saves about 10% FLOPs but loses about 0.5 pp, and the interpolation overhead eats some of the gain.

cruxes: What is the per-seed accuracy std and the run-to-run time noise (I005)? This decides how much margin above 0.753 is needed.
How many epochs does the port need to reach 0.753: about 10, or more? This sets the baseline feasible time.
What fraction of the 9.4 s is fixed cost and launch overhead rather than GPU compute? This determines whether compile and graphs can give more than 10%.
